kindExtra: Key shape for this task: a hand-written `hidden/issues.test.js` (add a second `tests` check for it) that asserts exactly the 24 ids once each, the three duplicate groups (each later id's `duplicateOf` is the oldest id and its action is `close`; the oldest has null), the two near-duplicates both null with different owners, the already-fixed issue closed with `1\.8\.2` in its reason, the security issue S1 + escalate + owner billing, the loud user-error issue not S1 or S2, the four planted needs-info ids with action `needs-info` and at most two others, the feature request labelled `enhancement|feature|request` and not `bug`, no web-owned issue below S1 with `fix-now`, and at least 20 of 24 owners equal to the CODEOWNERS team of the issue's area. Block-key `text` items: the security reason has `tenant|another (customer|user|account)|cross` and `private`; the user-error reason has `browser|unsupported`; the two asked facts the document states (`1\.9` near `freez|frozen|release`; `4 ?h(ours)?|four hours` near `S1|security`). One `evidence` item: at least 10 valid citations into `issues/`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `CODEOWNERS`. Severity of the ordinary S2/S3 bugs is not keyed (reasonable people differ); the rubric covers it.

facts.answer: 1.9 is frozen for the Friday release. Only S1 fixes go into it; everything else waits for 1.10.
An S1 security issue must have an owner within 4 hours and goes to the private tracker, not the public one.
The web team is at a conference all week with no capacity. Schedule their work; only an S1 gets fix-now.

brief: Phase: issue triage. Role: developer (this week's triage owner). Folder: an issue tracker export of 24 open issues (`issues/ISSUE-401.md` to `ISSUE-424.md`, one file each: title, reporter, date, body, environment lines, comments, reaction count, in realistic voices: terse, angry, vague, precise), `CODEOWNERS` mapping `src/api/` to platform-api, `src/web/` to web, `src/billing/` to billing, `infra/` to sre, `docs/` to docs, `CHANGELOG.md` with an entry '1.8.2: fixed the CSV export dropping the last row', `docs/severity.md` (S1 data loss or security; S2 feature broken, no workaround; S3 workaround exists; S4 cosmetic; the labels in use), `docs/triage-process.md` (needs-info when there is no reproduction; a duplicate closes pointing at the oldest; security reports move to the private tracker), and enough real `src/` paths to resolve every issue's area. Plant: three duplicate groups {401, 409, 417} (export button hangs; 401 oldest), {404, 420} (login loop on Safari), {411, 423} (invoice footer typo); two near-duplicates that are not the same, 406 (upload fails over 10 MB on web) and 415 (upload fails on iOS at any size, different area); 408 already fixed (CSV last row dropped on 1.8.1, closed by 1.8.2); 413 a casually worded security report ('funny, I saw someone else's invoice when I changed the id') that is S1, escalate, owner billing; 419 the loudest issue (34 reactions, 'app crashes on start') whose environment line shows an unsupported browser and whose comment confirms it works on a supported one; four needs-info issues (no version, no steps, screenshot only); 421 a feature request filed as a bug; the rest ordinary S2 and S3 bugs with clear areas, several owned by web. The request asks for severity, labels, owner, duplicateOf and action for every issue, a short reason per issue citing evidence, the document at the given path ending with the JSON block. The request must not name the ladder rules, the duplicates, the security issue or the decoy. The lazy answer marks everything S3 schedule under platform-api; the copy answer pastes the titles; both must fail. The three scripted facts (which release is frozen, the S1 security SLA, the web team's capacity) are not in the folder; the reference asks for them and applies them (web-owned S2/S3 issues get `schedule`).
